finding.summary: Jinja vulnerable to HTML attribute injection when passing user input as keys to xmlattr filter

verdict.reasoning: The xmlattr filter is vulnerable when user-supplied input is used as attribute keys (not just values). In app.py:7-10, the /embed/signup route builds `attrs` directly from `request.args` keys (excluding only 'list'), meaning an attacker fully controls the dict keys passed to the template. templates/signup.html:3 applies the `xmlattr` filter to this dict, which is exactly the unsafe usage pattern described in the advisory. This is a public, unauthenticated route (no auth decorator shown) rendering output to other users ('Partners customise the embedded form'), satisfying the advisory's XSS precondition of attacker-controlled keys rendered in pages others view. Since user input flows unsanitized from request.args keys into the xmlattr filter, the vulnerable code path is directly reachable.

evidence.explanation: Builds attrs dict using arbitrary user-supplied query parameter names as keys, excluding only 'list'.
Passes the attacker-controlled attrs dict into the signup.html template render.
Applies the xmlattr filter to the attrs dict, which uses untrusted keys as HTML attribute names, matching the advisory's vulnerable pattern.
Exposes signup_widget as a public Flask route, making the input externally attacker-controllable.

GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95 (CVE-2024-22195)
package: jinja2
summary: Jinja vulnerable to HTML attribute injection when passing user input as keys to xmlattr filter
affected: >=0, <3.1.3

GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95 (jinja2) details:
The `xmlattr` filter in affected versions of Jinja accepts keys containing spaces. XML/HTML attributes cannot contain spaces, as each would then be interpreted as a separate attribute. If an application accepts keys (as opposed to only values) as user input, and renders these in pages that other users see as well, an attacker could use this to inject other attributes and perform XSS. Note that accepting keys as user input is not common or a particularly intended use case of the `xmlattr` filter, and an application doing so should already be verifying what keys are provided regardless of this fix.

GHSA-h75v-3vvj-5mfj (CVE-2024-34064)
package: jinja2
summary: Jinja vulnerable to HTML attribute injection when passing user input as keys to xmlattr filter
affected: >=0, <3.1.4

GHSA-h75v-3vvj-5mfj (jinja2) details:
The `xmlattr` filter in affected versions of Jinja accepts keys containing non-attribute characters. XML/HTML attributes cannot contain spaces, `/`, `>`, or `=`, as each would then be interpreted as starting a separate attribute. If an application accepts keys (as opposed to only values) as user input, and renders these in pages that other users see as well, an attacker could use this to inject other attributes and perform XSS. The fix for the previous GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95 CVE-2024-22195 only addressed spaces but not other characters.

Accepting keys as user input is now explicitly considered an unintended use case of the `xmlattr` filter, and code that does so without otherwise validating the input should be flagged as insecure, regardless of Jinja version. Accepting _values_ as user input continues to be safe.
